title: Verb (+ object) + to ... (I want you to ...)
subtitle: I want you to ... / make somebody do
summary: Use verb + somebody + to ... (want you to go, told me to wait) and remember that make and let take the bare infinitive (make him wait).

left.label: verb + to ...
left.text: want, expect, ask, help, would like, would prefer

right.label: verb + object + to ...
right.text: want somebody to, expect somebody to, ask somebody to, help somebody to ...
examples: **Would you like me to go** now?

lesson.heading: Not 'want that'; help with or without to
lesson.text: We do not usually say 'want that'. You can use **help** with or without to.

examples.text: Do you **want me to come** with you?
Can you **help me to move** this table?
examples.note: or Can you help me move this table?

lesson.heading: tell / advise / remind somebody to ...
lesson.text: These verbs have the structure **verb + object + to ...**: **tell, advise, remind, warn, invite, encourage, persuade, get, force, teach, allow, enable**. The verb can also be passive: *I was warned ... / we are allowed ...*.

examples.text: It's not a nice hotel. I wouldn't **advise you to stay** there.
Can you **remind me to call** Sam tomorrow?
Joe said the switch was dangerous and **warned me not to touch** it.
I didn't move the piano by myself. I **got somebody to help** me.
They don't **allow people to park** in front of the building.
I **was warned not to touch** the switch. / Are we **allowed to park** here?

lesson.heading: suggest
lesson.text: We do not use **suggest** with to ... . Use a *that* clause instead.

examples.text: Jane **suggested that I ask** you for advice.

lesson.heading: make somebody do / let somebody do
lesson.text: We say **make somebody do something** and **let somebody do something** - without to. But in the passive we say **(be) made to do** - with to.

examples.text: I **made him promise** that he wouldn't tell anybody what happened.
Her parents wouldn't **let her go** out alone.
examples.note: = wouldn't allow her to go out

examples.text: **Let me carry** your bag for you.
We **were made to wait** for two hours.

lesson.text: make and let are the two exceptions: make him wait, let her go - no to. Almost every other verb in this group (allow, force, persuade, tell ...) needs somebody + to ...

exercises.prompt: Do you have enough money, or do you want ___ you some?
exercises.explanation: want + object + to ...: do you want me to lend you some?

exercises.prompt: Shall I leave the window open, or would you like ___ it?
exercises.explanation: would like + object + to ...: would you like me to shut it?

exercises.prompt: 'Why don't you come and stay with us?' 'That would be nice.' They invited him ___.
exercises.explanation: invite somebody to ...: invited him to stay with them.

exercises.prompt: 'Don't forget to call Joe.' 'No, I won't forget.' He reminded her ___.
exercises.explanation: remind somebody to ...: reminded her to call Joe.

exercises.prompt: 'Be careful.' 'Don't worry. I will.' She warned ___.
exercises.explanation: warn somebody to ...: warned him to be careful.

exercises.prompt: After which verbs do we use somebody + to do, and after which somebody + do (no to)?
I was surprised that it rained. Say this with expect.
exercises.answer: I didn't expect it to rain.
exercises.explanation: expect + object + to ...: I didn't expect it to rain.

exercises.prompt: The film was very sad. It made me ___.
exercises.explanation: make somebody do - without to: made me cry.

exercises.prompt: Lisa's parents always encouraged her ___ hard at school.
exercises.explanation: encourage somebody to ...: encouraged her to study.

exercises.prompt: My lawyer said I shouldn't say anything to the police. Say this with advise.
exercises.answer: My lawyer advised me not to say anything to the police.
exercises.explanation: advise somebody not to ...: advised me not to say anything.

exercises.prompt: Sarah won't let me ___ her car. She doesn't trust me.
exercises.explanation: let somebody do - without to: let me drive.

exercises.statement: Jane suggested me to ask you for advice.
exercises.explanation: Jane suggested that I ask you for advice. We do not use suggest + somebody + to ...
